Cardtype: Vampire
Clan: Nosferatu
Capacity: 9
Discipline: cel dem ANI OBF POT
Camarilla Prince of Seattle: Casino may move up to 3 blood from

Does Casino's +damage ability apply to non-carded strikes (eg

check.

thanks,

> Joshua Duffin wrote:
> > Casino Reeds

> > (if so, it's a rather stronger ability than Joaquin Murrieta's...)

>
> mmm Murietta has a free additional strike in case you didn't notice ;)

Yes, *that* part of Murietta's ability is pretty strong. :-) But the
+damage for guns part is *way* less good than Casino's +damage ability.
And it seems odd that Casino gets charged a lot less points for his
abilities than Joaquin does:

Casino: 9 capacity Nosferatu
8 points of disciplines
Prince title (1 pt)
+damage ability (1 pt?)
blood-moving ability (1 pt?)

Joaquin: 9 capacity Toreador
7 points of disciplines (and only 2 superiors)
no title (0 pts)
additional strike ability (1 pt - Jacko seems to have paid 1 pt for his
version of this under the Sabbat costing scheme, and Jacko's even
stacks with other add'l strike effects)
+damage ability (should be 0.5 pts at most if Casino's is 1 pt - much
more limited)

That is, Joaquin "should" also have 11 pts of stuff (under the current
vampire-costing scheme), but instead has 8.5 or 9 at most (if you count
both abilities as 1 pt each). Seems to me like he should really have
about two more points of disciplines (increasing his superior count
to 4, maybe?).

Then again, Melisande would have to have been charged 2 pts for her
optional additional strike if she was also designed under the current
costing scheme (11 pts for 9-cap vampires, that is).

That really doesn't make sense to me, though, since the most widely
usable strong abilities have been costed at only 1 point each (+1
bleed, +1 strength, +1 intercept, +1 stealth) ever since Dark
Sovereigns, or Sabbat at the latest. (Rebekka, Muaziz, Jost Werner,
Kite, etc etc.) An optional additional strike just doesn't seem
plausibly better than one of those abilities to me.

Josh

the art (not science apparently) of vampire design

Messages.Author: Joshua Duffin
Messages.Body:
"LSJ" <vte...@white-wolf.com> wrote in message
news:3D663E26...@white-wolf.com...

> Joshua Duffin wrote:
> > That really doesn't make sense to me, though, since the most widely
> > usable strong abilities have been costed at only 1 point each (+1
> > bleed, +1 strength, +1 intercept, +1 stealth) ever since Dark
>
> Typically (current RT):
>
> +1 intercept is 1 point.
> +1 strength or bleed is 1.5 points.
> +1 stealth is 2 points.

Seems reasonable given that stealth is usually more "winning" than
intercept. Still, Jost Werner sure didn't pay 2 points for his
+1 stealth, although Lucretia paid at least 2. :-)

> The formula is *a* metric by which vampires can be measured. It
> is not the alpha and the omega of vampire design, however.

Clearly. Nor do I mean to dispute that vampire design *is* as much
art as science - a vampire with OBF FOR NEC and an optional additional
strike each combat would have a lot less use for that additional
strike than one with POT PRO VIC.

I have been surprised, though, to see how many vampires in CE *do*
seem somewhat inconsistent (typically looking underpowered next
to their more-interesting counterparts) in their "points".

Joaquin Murrieta is certainly an example; sure, CEL and an optional
additional make his combat-oriented abilities pretty good. But
Casino Reeds has POT cel as well, and his +damage ability is a
lot more general than Joaquin's, and he's a Prince *and* has more
points of disciplines. It just seems inexplicable from what I can
see - it'd make more sense if Joaquin had some out of clan (or
another in-clan) superiors, for example.

It's also struck me that the old justicars seemed more likely to
be the members of their clan with really great abilities than the
new ones are - eg Anneke with the "block any vampire" vs Madame
Guil (justicar, if I'm remembering the name right) with just +1
bleed (which Anneke also has) vs Helena *untitled) with the "may
burn a blood to be able to block and play Auspex reaction cards
as if untapped" ability. Which is probably not a bad thing at
all, since it makes the non-prince/justicar vamps more relatively
worthwhile - it's just different. I think.

Josh

are at home...

Jaroslav, Cock Robin, and Maris Streck seem to be the new *power* justicars
(compared to the old Anneke and Sheldon).

Lucinde and Madame Guil are a lot more vanilla. They're not god-awful-bad like
the last group, but probably fit more into mediocre justicars (a la Ulugh, Don
Cruez, and Lucian).

There fortunately aren't any REAL bad justicars this time like Democritus and
Angus (I paid how much and I still only have inferior Fortitude?).

I'm still exactly not sure where Anastasz fits in. I know Xian is ecstatic
about an 8-cap Justicar but...
